description: This course explores human responses to epidemic diseases in world history. Beginning with the
pandemics of the Ancient world, students encounter the 14th-century Black Death, "virgin soil"
epidemics in the Americas, London's cholera outbreak of the 1850s, as well as more recent events,
from the 1918 influenza pandemic to Covid-19. Students consider the varied medical, social,
political, and cultural impacts of disease through an exploration of diverse topics, ranging from
the discovery of microbes to the recent popularity of zombie movies. Offered periodically during
fullname: Plagues and Peoples in World History
